relationship_to_restored_text: Interpretive contemplative layer aligned by verse. This does not replace the source-audited restored translation.

verses.mystical_translation: Levi's household begins through Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
Kohath's four sons establish another branch.
Miriam stands beside Aaron and Moses before the priestly line narrows toward sons.
Eleazar's line continues through Phinehas and Abishua.
Bukki and Uzzi carry the line.
Zerahiah and Meraioth follow.
Amariah and Ahitub follow.
Zadok and Ahimaaz follow.
Azariah and Johanan follow.
Priestly service is attached to Solomon's temple.
The line continues through another Amariah and Ahitub.
Zadok and Shallum continue it.
Hilkiah and Azariah continue it.
Seraiah and Jehozadak stand near the exile.
A priestly family is carried away with Jerusalem under Babylonian power.
Levi's three sons are named again as the archive restarts.
Gershom's sons are Libni and Shimei.
Kohath's sons are repeated.
Merari's sons complete the three family branches.
Libni, Jahath, and Zimmah begin Gershom's descent.
Joah, Iddo, Zerah, and Jeatherai continue it.
Kohath's line moves through Amminadab, Korah, and Assir.
Elkanah, Ebiasaph, and Assir continue.
Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul continue.
Amasai and Ahimoth are named as Elkanah's sons.
Another Elkanah line moves through Zophai and Nahath.
Eliab, Jeroham, and Elkanah approach Samuel's household.
Samuel's sons are remembered through a text whose first name remains disputed.
Merari's line moves through Mahli, Libni, Shimei, and Uzzah.
Shimea, Haggiah, and Asaiah complete it.
David organizes singers after the ark comes to rest.
Music becomes continuous service from tent to temple.
Heman's musical household is traced back toward Samuel.
The singer's ancestry continues through Elkanah and Jeroham.
More generations preserve the musical line.
The genealogy continues through Joel, Azariah, and Zephaniah.
Korah's descendants remain within worship despite ancestral conflict.
The line reaches Levi and Israel.
Asaph stands beside Heman, with his own remembered ancestry.
Michael, Baaseiah, and Malchijah continue Asaph's line.
Ethni, Zerah, and Adaiah continue it.
Ethan, Zimmah, and Shimei continue it.
Jahath, Gershom, and Levi close Asaph's ancestry.
Ethan and Merari's descendants stand on the other side of the singers.
Hashabiah, Amaziah, and Hilkiah continue the line.
Amzi, Bani, and Shemer continue it.
Mahli, Mushi, Merari, and Levi close it.
Other Levites sustain every form of tabernacle service beyond public song.
Aaron's household carries altar and atonement work within Israel's ritual order.
The priestly ancestry is repeated from Eleazar through Abishua.
Bukki, Uzzi, and Zerahiah continue.
Meraioth, Amariah, and Ahitub continue.
Zadok and Ahimaaz close this priestly line.
The genealogy becomes a map of homes and pasturelands.
Hebron is shared with priestly families.
Caleb's fields and villages remain separately remembered.
A city of refuge and several towns support Aaron's descendants.
Holon and Debir are added with pasturelands.
Ashan and Beth-shemesh are added.
Benjamin contributes Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth.
Remaining Kohathites receive ten cities from half-Manasseh.
Gershom's families receive thirteen cities across four tribes.
Merari's families receive twelve cities across three tribes.
Israel's tribes sustain Levite households with cities and pasture.
Lots distribute named towns from Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin.
Kohathite families also receive towns in Ephraim.
Shechem's refuge function stands beside Gezer's pasturelands.
Jokmeam and Beth-horon join the network.
Aijalon and Gath-rimmon join it.
Aner and Bileam support remaining Kohathites.
Golan and Ashtaroth support Gershom's families.
Kedesh and Daberath come from Issachar.
Ramoth and Anem come with them.
Mashal and Abdon come from Asher.
Hukok and Rehob come with them.
Naphtali gives Kedesh, Hammon, and Kiriathaim.
Zebulun gives Rimmon and Tabor to Merari's descendants.
Reuben gives Bezer and Jahzah east of Jordan.
Kedemoth and Mephaath join them.
Gad gives Ramoth-gilead and Mahanaim.
Heshbon and Jazer complete the Levitical city network.

contemplative_note: Worship appears here as an ecosystem: prophets, priests, singers, carriers, gatekeepers, cooks, treasurers, towns, pasture, and refuge. Holiness is not concentrated in one prestigious office. It depends on distributed labor and shared land—and therefore requires accountability to everyone whose work makes sacred life possible.
